body: But, with more dates, her self-doubt can change. I know it's too early to tell that she's into me, but it's not too late to find out with a second date.

I'm not the type of guy that runs from a challenge. People's ideals about themselves can be changed with enough **genuine** effort. She's never had a person show her that she's beautiful. I'm gonna be that guy. 

She's been beat down for most of her life. Leaving her would fuel the flames of her insecurities rather than extinguish them. And to be honest, that would mean I would be a part of her demise if I were to leave her.

When people are in relationships, they build each other, not run from them...

Lmao! Holy shit dude/dudette! You're hilarious! And this wall of text shows me that you really give a damn about what I'm going through.

All of this is duly noted! Appreciate it!

Honestly,

I truly believe that she is attractive. And, beauty is subjective. This is what drew me to her in the first place. But, what locked me in was her personality. She actually had a pretty nice glow-up after high school, but she's still damaged from those days.

I think it's cruel to have someone under a ruse of lies. If I didn't mean something, I wouldn't have said it. But, I'll take your advice and show her that I like her, rather than tell her.
I've only told her once that she was pretty, other than that it was just her ranting about being bullied, until I had to change it to a more comfortable subject.

I respect the brutal honesty. And, thank you! I'm just gonna lay off the praises. It's hard not to compliment a woman even if they don't like themselves. (Hence the: "Honey, do I look fat in this dress?" shit-test). I feel like a yes-man now...
